newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN gives prize to Handicap International.
newsitem.headline: UN gives prize to Handicap International.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency announced on Tuesday it was awarding its annual Nansen Medal to Handicap International, a Franco-Belgian group which makes artifical limbs for landmine victims worldwide.
Sadako Ogata, U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees UNHCR), would present a $100,000 cheque on Friday to Dr.Jean-Baptiste Richardier, co-founder and co-director of the group, the UNHCR office said.
Patrick Segal, Handicap International's vice president and France's inter-ministerial delegate for handicapped people, would attend the ceremony in Geneva.

In a statement, Ogata praised Handicap International, a non-governmental organisation based in Lyon, France, for its outstanding work with refugees and enormous contribution to the growing campaign for a total ban on anti-personnel landmines. Mines are a major menace for refugees being repatriated.
"Without Handicap International, hundreds of handicapped refugees from Cambodia, Mozambique and Bosnia could not have started a new life," she said.

Handicap International provides prostheses to war victims, largely manufactured in the area using local materials, according to UNHCR. Two of its staff have been killed in the field, one in Afghanistan in 1989 and the other in northern Iraq in 1993.
Established in 1982 in response to the refugee crisis in Cambodia, the group is now active in 35 countries and works closely with UNHCR on programmes for handicapped refugees and returnees.

The Nansen award is named after the Norwegian diplomat and explorer Fridtjof Nansen, the first High Commissioner for Refugees under the League of Nations. It includes a $100,000 gift from Norway, to be spent on a project for refugees.
Previous laureates include Mozambique's Graca Machel (1995), and Medecins Sans Frontieres (Doctors Without Borders) in 1993.
